_source: UX-P166 — real production payloads, pulled 2026-08-29 from GET /api/events/{id}
on the deployed build. Not hand-authored: the `opening_odds` and `current_odds`
blocks below are verbatim what the endpoint served, and the `naive_*` fields
record what the shipped surfaces printed from them BEFORE this queue.
WHY BARCELONA IS THE EXEMPLAR. Its `opening_odds` and `current_odds` hold the
SAME two floats — 0.845 home, 0.155 away. The card printed `85/15` from
current_odds (which carries the server's rendered percents) and `Opened 85/16`
from opening_odds (which carries none), so one card disagreed with itself about
one pair of numbers. The fix already existed one field over.
POPULATION (db-query over `events`, same day): every one of the 24,117 events
carrying an opening line is a complement pair, and 207 print 101 — 115

events.$why: THE EXEMPLAR — the identical float pair printed 85/15 from one field and 85/16 from the other, on the same card. 0.155 * 100 is 15.500000000000002 in IEEE 754, so half-up takes it to 16 while the favourite's own 84.5 goes to 85.

THE ONE THAT WAS LIVE WHEN THIS WAS MEASURED — the single live 101 in the census. The AWAY side is the favourite here, so the derived point lands on HOME and the home number moves 32 -> 31. That is the favourite-survives rule doing the thing always-away-first would get wrong in the other direction.

The 0.625 / 0.375 pair the handover directive predicted as the latent shape. It is not latent: this event is in the census, and both 62.5 and 37.5 are exactly representable so BOTH sides round up with no floating-point excuse.

THE LEAVE-ALONE DIRECTION (gotcha #43), and a real row rather than a constructed one. An ordinary complement pair not on a .5 boundary — 23,910 of the 24,117 — must print exactly what it printed before. A guard whose tests only prove it fires is how a diversity cap emptied the Sports tab.

SYNTHETIC, and labelled as such — no event in the measured population is out of band, so the only way to pin the out-of-band branch is to construct one. A pair summing to 0.97 must NOT be forced to 100: normalizing it would invent three points of probability rather than round one. Same value as the card_sum_reason exemplar in contracts/rendered_percent.json.
